chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who prayed five [rakʿahs], and he said: “If he had sat in the fourth [rakʿah] for the measure of the tashahhud, then his salat (prayer) is complete.”

So it is not contrary to the first report, because whoever sat in the fourth [rakʿah] and then stood and prayed one rakʿah did not omit any pillar from the pillars of the salat (prayer); rather, he only failed regarding the taslim, and failure regarding the taslim does not necessitate repeating the salat (prayer), according to what we have stated before. And whenever he doubts between the fourth and the fifth, he builds upon the fourth, gives taslim, and performs the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, and they are the two humiliators [of Shaytan].

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the closing salutation ending the prayer
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the prescribed testimony recited in the sitting of prayer
key_terms.الرَّابِعَةِ: the fourth rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.الْمُرْغِمَتَانِ: a designation for the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, meaning the two acts that abase
key_terms.تَمَّتْ صَلَاتُهُ: his prayer is considered complete and valid
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.صَلَّى خَمْسًا: performed five rakʿahs in the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays a fifth rakʿah or doubts between the fourth and fifth in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of one who mistakenly performs a fifth rakʿah in salat (prayer). If he had already sat in the fourth for the measure of tashahhud, his prayer remains valid, and if he doubts between the fourth and fifth, he should treat it as the fourth, give taslim, and perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.
